title: Understanding P-Values and Statistical Significance in Hypothesis Testing

cues.en: -: Hello, and welcome back to the course.
cues.zh: 大家好，歡迎回到課程。

cues.en: Today, we're talking about P values and statistical significance.
cues.zh: 今天要談 p 值與統計顯著性。

cues.en: A quick heads up, this tutorial is borrowed from another course of ours called "Statistics for Business Analytics and Data Science A to Z".
cues.zh: 先提醒，這堂借用自我們另一門課，Statistics for Business Analytics and Data Science A-Z。

cues.en: If you hear references to Z score and hypothesis testing and other parts that are relevant to that course
cues.zh: 如果聽到 z 分數、假設檢定，或其他與那門課有關，

cues.en: but not relevant to the course in which we're in right now, then please ignore them.
cues.zh: 但與目前課程無關的引用，先忽略即可。

cues.en: The focus of this tutorial, what we want to get out of it, is P values, what they mean, how to feel about them, and what statistical significance means,
cues.zh: 這堂重點是 p 值的意義、如何直覺理解它，以及統計顯著性，

cues.en: and what hypothesis testing is all about.
cues.zh: 還有假設檢定究竟在做什麼。

cues.en: So with that in mind, here we go.
cues.zh: 記住這些目標，開始吧。

cues.en: Hello, and welcome back to the course on statistics.
cues.zh: 大家好，歡迎回到統計課程。

cues.en: Today, we've got a very exciting topic, statistical significance, and it's very exciting, because I know that from my experience from my career
cues.zh: 今天有個很精彩的主題，統計顯著性。根據我的工作經驗，

cues.en: it's a question that is always asked.
cues.zh: 這是一個總會被問到的問題。

cues.en: Or at least you ask yourself this question, Is my results statistically significant or not?
cues.zh: 至少你會問自己：我的結果是否達到統計顯著？

cues.en: Or are these insights statistically significant or not?
cues.zh: 這些發現有統計顯著性嗎？

cues.en: And if you don't understand statistical significance, then it's a question that you dread from your manager or the person that you're reporting to, because you cannot substantiate your results.
cues.zh: 如果不理解，就會害怕主管或報告對象問這個問題，因為無法替結果提出根據。

cues.en: You found some stuff, but you don't know if it's right or wrong.
cues.zh: 你找到一些東西，卻不知道是否可靠。

cues.en: And in this section, we're gonna be exploring this concept in a lot of detail, and we're going to be referencing it a lot, and you will get a great understanding.
cues.zh: 這一節會深入探討，也會經常引用這個概念，幫你建立理解。

cues.en: Hopefully, you'll be able to build a strong understanding of statistical significance.
cues.zh: 希望你能充分掌握統計顯著性。

cues.en: However, in this tutorial, what we're gonna focus on is on the intuition behind statistical significance.
cues.zh: 但這堂先聚焦背後的直覺。

cues.en: How you can link how you feel about an experiment to what actually statistical significance is.
cues.zh: 如何把自己對實驗的感受，與真正的統計顯著性連結。

cues.en: So let's have a look.
cues.zh: 來看看。

cues.en: All right, so here we've got an experiment, a coin toss.
cues.zh: 這裡是一個擲硬幣實驗。

cues.en: I know it's always a coin toss, but a coin toss is, in all fairness, a great example to get started with, because it is so simple.
cues.zh: 我知道又是硬幣，但它確實很適合作為起點，因為非常簡單。

cues.en: There's only two possible outcomes, and you've already done this so many times in your life that you know kind of what to expect, and that's why it will help us build the intuition.
cues.zh: 只有兩種結果，而且人生中已擲過很多次，大概知道會發生什麼，所以能幫助建立直覺。

cues.en: So there are two possible versions or two possible situations kind of like...
cues.zh: 有兩個可能的版本，或兩種情境。

cues.en: We're gonna start talking about hypothesis testing right now.
cues.zh: 現在開始談假設檢定。

cues.en: When we're talking about hypothesis testing, we're thinking about two possible alternative universes, if you will, if you want to put it that way.
cues.zh: 做假設檢定時，可以把它想成兩個不同的平行宇宙。

cues.en: So one possible universe is that, in that universe, it's a fair coin in that scenario, in that environment, but probably, I like the way to put it as in the universe.
cues.zh: 其中一個宇宙裡，硬幣是公平的；在那種情境、環境裡，但我比較喜歡說成宇宙。

cues.en: So in that universe, it's a fair coin.
cues.zh: 所以，在這個宇宙裡，硬幣公平。

cues.en: So that's our original assumption.
cues.zh: 這是最初的假設。

cues.en: That's why it's got H-0.
cues.zh: 因此標記為 H0。

cues.en: That's the null hypothesis that we are starting off with.
cues.zh: 也就是我們出發時的虛無假設。

cues.en: And then H-1 is the alternative universe or the alternative hypothesis, sometimes also called H-A.
cues.zh: H1 則是另一個宇宙，或對立假設，有時也記為 HA。

cues.en: And in this universe, this is not a fair point.
cues.zh: 在那個宇宙裡，硬幣不公平。

cues.en: So we want to understand which universe do we live in, or which situation are we actually dealing with, or what is the truth.
cues.zh: 我們要了解，自己究竟活在哪個宇宙，面對哪種情境，真相是什麼。

cues.en: That's what we're trying to assess.
cues.zh: 這就是要判斷的事。

cues.en: Is it a fair coin, is the null hypothesis correct?
cues.zh: 硬幣公平，虛無假設正確嗎？

cues.en: Or is it not a fair coin, and then the alternative hypothesis is correct.
cues.zh: 還是不公平，因此對立假設正確？

cues.en: And so the way we're gonna go about this is we're going to assume that H-0 or the null hypothesis is true.
cues.zh: 做法是，先假設 H0，也就是虛無假設成立。

cues.en: So we're going to assume that we live in the first universe.
cues.zh: 假設自己位於第一個宇宙。

cues.en: And then based on our experiment, we're going to see if we can contradict that, if we can come to a contradiction and say, oh, actually, our assumption was incorrect.
cues.zh: 再根據實驗，看看是否能得到矛盾，指出原先的假設其實不正確。

cues.en: And we'll talk more about that towards the end of this tutorial.
cues.zh: 這堂課最後會再談。

cues.en: But for now, let's assume that you've got a coin that you're tossing or somebody's gonna toss just now, and you're assuming it's a fair coin.
cues.zh: 目前先假設你或別人正要擲一枚硬幣，而且你認為它是公平的。

cues.en: We live in that universe.
cues.zh: 我們位於這個宇宙。

cues.en: So the coin is tossed the first time, and the result is tails.
cues.zh: 第一次投擲，結果是反面。

cues.en: The question is, how do you feel about this?
cues.zh: 你有什麼感覺？

cues.en: Forget about our statistics for a second.
cues.zh: 先忘掉統計。

cues.en: How do you feel about this?
cues.zh: 你怎麼想？

cues.en: Do you feel that this is a fair coin or the coin is rigged?
cues.zh: 覺得硬幣公平，還是被動過手腳？

cues.en: You probably feel that it is likely a fair coin.
cues.zh: 你大概覺得它應該公平。

cues.en: This is a totally probable outcome.
cues.zh: 這是完全可能的結果。

cues.en: In that universe that we have assumed we live in, in the H-0 universe, the probability of that is 50%.
cues.zh: 在假設的 H0 宇宙裡，機率是 50%。

cues.en: So it could have been heads, could have been tails, no problem.
cues.zh: 正面、反面都有可能，沒問題。

cues.en: Then, the coin is tossed a second time and it's tails again.
cues.zh: 第二次擲，又是反面。

cues.en: How do you feel about this now?
cues.zh: 現在有什麼感覺？

cues.en: Do you feel that the coin is rigged, or do you feel that it's a fair coin?
cues.zh: 覺得有問題，還是仍然公平？

cues.en: Well, let's look at the probability of this happening in our universe that we're living in.
cues.zh: 看看在目前假設的宇宙裡，這件事發生的機率。

cues.en: In the H-0 hypothesis, the probability of that happening if this is a fair coin is 25%.
cues.zh: 在 H0 成立、硬幣公平時，這種情況的機率是 25%。

cues.en: So no big deal, could happen.
cues.zh: 沒什麼大不了，可能發生。

cues.en: Then, the coin is tossed again, and again, it's tails.
cues.zh: 再擲一次，又是反面。

cues.en: Okay, so how do you feel about that now?
cues.zh: 現在感覺如何？

cues.en: What do you feel about having three coins, three times the same coin is tossed, and you get every single time it's tails?
cues.zh: 同一枚硬幣連擲三次，每次都是反面，你怎麼想？

cues.en: Well, it might be a bit suspicious, but it's fairly okay, because in our universe in which we live in, in the H-0 universe where the coin is assumed to be fair,
cues.zh: 可能有點可疑，但還算可以接受，因為在假設硬幣公平的 H0 宇宙裡，

cues.en: this could have happened, and the probability of that happening is 12%.
cues.zh: 它仍可能發生，機率大約 12%。

cues.en: But then, the coin is tossed again, and guess what?
cues.zh: 接著再擲一次，猜怎麼樣？

cues.en: It's tails again.
cues.zh: 又是反面。

cues.en: All right, so are you getting a bit suspicious now?
cues.zh: 現在開始懷疑了嗎？

cues.en: Do you feel that if this were a fair coin this would be quite hard for this to happen?
cues.zh: 如果硬幣公平，你覺得這種情況是不是不太容易發生？

cues.en: Well, in the universe that we assume we live in, in the H-0 universe where the null hypothesis is assumed to be true or where the null hypothesis is true,
cues.zh: 在假設虛無假設成立的 H0 宇宙裡，

cues.en: and we assume we're in that universe, well, in that case, this could have happened with a probability of 6%.
cues.zh: 這件事的機率大約是 6%。

cues.en: All right, and then the coin is tossed again, and again, it is tales.
cues.zh: 接著又擲一次，仍然是反面。

cues.en: Now, how do you feel about it?
cues.zh: 現在怎麼想？

cues.en: How do you feel about seeing somebody toss a coin and them getting tails every single time, five times in a row?
cues.zh: 看到有人連續擲五次，每次都是反面，你的感覺如何？

cues.en: Well, you feel a bit, correct me if I'm wrong, but I'm assuming you feel a bit uneasy about that, that you feel that something might be going on here,
cues.zh: 如果我猜錯請更正，但我想你開始不太放心，覺得這裡可能有問題，

cues.en: something is a bit not right.
cues.zh: 哪裡不太對勁。

cues.en: It's a bit suspicious that this coin has had tails five times in a row.
cues.zh: 連續五次反面，確實有點可疑。

cues.en: And your feeling is correct, your feeling is natural, because the probability of this happening, if we assume that it is a fair coin, the probability of this happening is only 3%.
cues.zh: 這種感覺很自然，因為假設硬幣公平，發生這種結果的機率只有大約 3%。

cues.en: So if we assume that we live in a universe where the null hypothesis is true, where the coin is a fair coin, we would've only seen this with a likelihood of 3%.
cues.zh: 也就是說，如果虛無假設成立、硬幣公平，這種結果只會以大約 3% 的機率出現。

cues.en: Meaning that you would have to watch this experiment on 33 different occasions.
cues.zh: 相當於要觀察這個實驗約 33 次。

cues.en: Like you watch it today, you watch it tomorrow, you watch it another day.
cues.zh: 例如今天看一次、明天看一次、後天再看一次。

cues.en: You would have to watch it on 33 different days or 33 different times this experiment of five coin toss would have to be conducted, and only once you would see this result.
cues.zh: 這個連擲五次的實驗，大約做 33 天，或做 33 次，才會看到一次這種結果。

cues.en: So it's a very low probability, and that's why your feeling of something's going on here is completely valid, completely justified.
cues.zh: 機率很低，所以你覺得有問題，是完全可以理解的。

cues.en: But then, let's see what happens.
cues.zh: 再看看接下來。

cues.en: The coin is tossed again, and this time it's, guess what, tails again (laughs).
cues.zh: 又擲了一次，猜猜，還是反面。

cues.en: I know you were probably expecting heads.
cues.zh: 我知道你可能期待正面。

cues.en: No, it's tails again.
cues.zh: 沒有，又是反面。

cues.en: What do you think is going on here?
cues.zh: 你覺得怎麼回事？

cues.en: How do you feel about this coin?
cues.zh: 對這枚硬幣有什麼感覺？

cues.en: Do you feel that it's still a fair coin?
cues.zh: 還認為它公平嗎？

cues.en: Do you feel that our assumption that it's a fair coin is correct?
cues.zh: 覺得原本公平硬幣的假設仍然正確嗎？

cues.en: Or do you feel uneasy about that assumption?
cues.zh: 還是對這個假設感到不安？

cues.en: Do you feel that something might be suspicious here?
cues.zh: 覺得可能有可疑之處嗎？

cues.en: And if you feel that something might be suspicious here, you are again very well justified even more than so than previously, because probability of that happening is about 1%, 1% only.
cues.zh: 如果覺得可疑，那比之前更有理由，因為這種結果的機率大約只有 1%。

cues.en: And then what is going on here is that the probability of this happening is dropping as you get more and more tails.
cues.zh: 每多一次反面，這種結果的機率就愈低。

cues.en: And in terms of this course and further down, we'll be operating with the term P value.
cues.zh: 接下來課程會使用 p 值這個詞。

cues.en: In fact, we've already seen P values when we looked at the Z score table previously when we were looking up the Z scores.
cues.zh: 其實前面查 z 分數表時，已經看過 p 值。

cues.en: Well, in that table in the middle, what you have is actually a P value.
cues.zh: 表格中間的數字，其實就是 p 值。

cues.en: So you can see that the P value is dropping.
cues.zh: 所以可以看到，p 值一直下降。

cues.en: That simply the probability of this happening, given that we are in a universe where the null hypothesis is true.
cues.zh: 這是在虛無假設成立的宇宙裡，這種結果發生的機率。

cues.en: And this is very important to understand that if we're in this universe, this top universe, then this is what the P value looks like.
cues.zh: 務必理解，在上面這個宇宙裡，p 值才會是這樣。

cues.en: It's very unlikely that you'll get six tails in a row.
cues.zh: 連續六次反面，非常不容易。

cues.en: However, if you think about it for a second, if we were in this universe where it's not a fair coin, where it's a, for example, it's a weighted coin or both sides of the coin are tails,
cues.zh: 但想一想，如果身處另一個宇宙，硬幣不公平，例如加了配重，或兩面都是反面，

cues.en: that if you have a coin like that, if we were in this universe then these P values would be completely different.
cues.zh: 那麼這些 p 值就會完全不同。

cues.en: They wouldn't be like this.
cues.zh: 不會像現在這樣。

cues.en: The P values would be a hundred percent, a hundred percent, hundred percent, hundred percent hundred percent, hundred percent.
So if we lived in this second universe, we wouldn't get that feeling.
cues.zh: 如果住在第二個宇宙，就不會有那種不安。

cues.en: We wouldn't get suspicious over here or even more suspicious over here.
cues.zh: 不會從這裡開始懷疑，再到這裡更懷疑。

cues.en: We would totally be comfortable with this, because we know that the coin has two tails on each side.
cues.zh: 因為已知道硬幣兩邊都是反面，所以會覺得很正常。

cues.en: There's a tails on the coin, and therefore, we would be totally comfortable with one tails in a row, two tails in a row, three, four, five, six tails in a row.
cues.zh: 兩面都是反面，連續一次、兩次、三次、四次、五次、六次反面，都很正常。

cues.en: We wouldn't get any uneasy feeling about it if we lived in this universe.
cues.zh: 在這個宇宙裡，完全不會不安。

cues.en: However, the way hypothesis testing works is that we assume we live in this universe over here at the top, the null hypothesis universe.
cues.zh: 但假設檢定的做法，是先假設住在上面的虛無假設宇宙。

cues.en: And then we want to see will we get, whatever our experiment is, will we get an uneasy feeling about it.
cues.zh: 再看看，不論實驗是什麼，是否會對結果產生不安。

cues.en: And this uneasy feeling in mathematical terms, you can't just go up to your boss and say, or your manager or your client, you can't just go and say, "I had an uneasy feeling about this.
cues.zh: 但不能直接對老闆、主管或客戶說：「我有點不安，

cues.en: I don't think it's true."
cues.zh: 所以覺得這不是真的。」

cues.en: Of course, you have to put in mathematical terms, and that's where statistical significance comes in.
cues.zh: 當然要用數學表達，這就是統計顯著性出場的地方。

cues.en: So statistical significance is basically this line over here, as simple as that, 5%.
cues.zh: 簡單來說，統計顯著性就是這條線，5%。

cues.en: So that's where you started getting this uneasy feeling.
cues.zh: 也就是開始感到不安的界線。

cues.en: Just after the 6%, you started being very suspicious about things going on, and that's about right.
cues.zh: 在 6% 之後，開始覺得事情很可疑，這大致符合直覺。

cues.en: That's because as soon as something is 5% or less likely to happen, that's the alpha here, then that is, 5% is like one out of 20.
cues.zh: 一旦某件事發生機率是 5% 或更低，這裡就是 α；5% 大約是二十分之一。

cues.en: So that's when we draw the line, and we say, okay, so that is, it's so unlikely.
cues.zh: 我們就在這裡劃線，認為結果實在太不可能。

cues.en: I am so unlikely to see this by random that I'm going to reject this null hypothesis.
cues.zh: 偶然看到這種結果的機率太低，因此拒絕虛無假設。

cues.en: I'm going to say that, because I'm seeing this and it was so unlikely to happen at random, this cannot be true.
cues.zh: 因為看到這種結果，而它隨機發生的機率很低，所以認為原假設不成立。

cues.en: And that's where you say that I'm confident, I'm rejecting this null hypothesis with 95% confidence.
cues.zh: 這時會說，以 95% 的信心水準拒絕虛無假設。

cues.en: That I'm 95% sure that we don't live in this universe.
cues.zh: 也就是我有 95% 的把握，認為不在這個宇宙。

cues.en: There's a 5% chance that we do, but I'm 95% sure that we don't live in this universe.
cues.zh: 雖然仍有 5% 的可能，但我有 95% 把握，認為不在這個宇宙。

cues.en: I'm going to reject that hypothesis, and I'm going to state that we live in a universe where this coin is actually rigged.
cues.zh: 因此拒絕這個假設，主張我們處於硬幣被動過手腳的宇宙。

cues.en: And you can set this confidence level to whatever you like.
cues.zh: 這個信心水準可以自行設定。

cues.en: You can set it to 10%.
cues.zh: 例如設成 10%。

cues.en: Then, you'd be rejecting over here.
cues.zh: 那就在這個位置拒絕。

cues.en: You can set it to 1%.
cues.zh: 也可以設成 1%。

cues.en: You could be rejecting over here.
cues.zh: 那就在這個位置拒絕。

cues.en: So it depends on your experiment.
cues.zh: 取決於實驗。

cues.en: Most of the time, 95 is a good level to go with, but sometimes, especially in medical trials and things like that where people's lives depend on that,
cues.zh: 大多數時候，95% 是常用水準，但有時，尤其醫療試驗等牽涉生命的情境，

cues.en: the results or the confirmation or not confirmation or whether or not we reject the null hypothesis, in those cases, you might want to,
cues.zh: 結果、確認與否，或是否拒絕虛無假設，都很重要，這時可能

cues.en: sometimes, it's required that you set it to 99%.
cues.zh: 會要求設成 99%。

cues.en: So it depends on your experiment and on what you're doing with those results.
cues.zh: 所以取決於實驗，以及結果的用途。

cues.en: But generally speaking, this is what statistical significance is all about.
cues.zh: 一般而言，統計顯著性就是這個概念。

cues.en: It's the point where in human intuitive terms you get uneasy about the null hypothesis being true, and you get super suspicious about it.
cues.zh: 用人的直覺來說，就是開始對虛無假設成立感到不安、非常懷疑的時候。

cues.en: In mathematical terms, it's just where you draw the line and you say, okay, I have enough confidence or this is sufficient level of confidence for me to reject the null hypothesis.
cues.zh: 用數學來說，就是設定一條界線，認為已有足夠的信心水準，可以拒絕虛無假設。

cues.en: So I actually am going to state that we live in this alternate universe.
cues.zh: 因此主張，我們處在另一個宇宙。
